Users who rely on encrypted HFS+ volumes won't need to decrypt their drives before converting them to APFS for compatibility with macOS 28. Here's what the change means.

Apple updates its macOS 28 upgrade guide with new guidance for encrypted HFS+ disks

A few weeks ago, Apple published a support document stating that starting with macOS 28, "Mac OS Extended is only supported on volumes that aren't encrypted (either the volume or the drive containing it)."

The change essentially means that users currently using encrypted HFS+ external drives or other volumes encrypted using the legacy Mac format would need to "decrypt or reformat any encrypted Mac OS Extended volumes," Apple explained.

Previously, the support page offered step-by-step instructions directing users to either decrypt the volume or erase and reformat it with APFS.

Apple has now updated the page to add a third option, allowing users to convert an encrypted HFS+ volume directly to encrypted APFS without decrypting it first. The company has also provided the following new steps:

Convert the volume to encrypted APFS

However, Apple notes that "this method doesn't apply to encrypted Time Machine backup volumes."

The company has also removed the previous instructions that involved first decrypting the volume, converting to APFS (without erasing data), and then optionally re-encrypting.

To view the updated support page, follow this link.

Will this new option make it easier for you to prepare your drive for the macOS 28 upgrade? Share your thoughts in the comments.
